En début de semaine, j’ai écrit un premi: Earlier this week, I wrote a first article on the disappearance of the federal ministry of Diversity, Inclusion and Persons with Disabilities. The decision has sparked outrage, but unfortunately it comes as no surprise to those most affected.

Dans le présent article, je m’intéresse: In this article, I look at the issues of diversity and inclusion, which are now the responsibility of the Ministry of Canadian Identity and Culture. The choice has been heavily criticized. Several observers fear a return to a universalist vision in Canada, in which a single identity, without regard for the differences among marginalized communities, would obscure their struggles. Others denounce the end of a “passing trend” that followed the emergence of equity and inclusion structures after the death of George Floyd in 2020.

At first glance, the Liberal government seems intent on continuing its predecessor’s efforts on inclusion. Yet one absence has not gone unnoticed: that of the Ministry of Diversity, Inclusion and Persons with Disabilities, which has simply disappeared. The decision is surprising, but for many in the field, it only confirms a trend observed time and again: a political retreat on questions of equity. Report.

A few months later in Canada, the death of Joyce Echaquan, an Atikamekw woman from Manawan, in a Quebec hospital revived calls for racial justice and equity. These tragedies had pushed several governments to review their inclusion policies.
Mais cinq ans plus tard, ces engagements: But five years later, those commitments seem to be running out of steam.
